## Understanding the Entropy of the Discrete Uniform Distribution
In this R script, we visualize the entropy of the discrete uniform distribution.  
The entropy of a probability distribution is used to estimate the unexpectedness 
of a probability distribution based on its parameters.  For the discrete uniform 
distribution, the entropy takes a logarithm form based on the number of outcomes (N).  
Hence, the rate of increase of the entropy will be greater in low values of 
N.  Additionally, the script provides visualizations of the probabililty mass 
function along with the entropy.  

```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# R Code to Visualize the Entropy of the Discrete Uniform Distribution
# ==============================================================================

# This script performs entropy calculations and generates plots to demonstrate
# the relationship between the number of outcomes and the entropy of a
# discrete uniform distribution.

# Install and load the 'ggplot2' package if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggplot2")
}
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1: Entropy Calculation for a Simple Example
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Let's calculate the entropy for a fair six-sided die.
# The number of possible outcomes, N, is 6.
N <- 6

# The entropy of a discrete uniform distribution is H(X) = log2(N).
entropy_value <- log2(N)

cat("--- Entropy Calculation for a Fair Six-Sided Die ---\n")
cat(paste("Number of outcomes (N):", N, "\n"))
cat(paste("Entropy H(Y) = log2(N) =", round(entropy_value, 4), "bits\n\n"))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 2: Visualization of Entropy vs. Number of Outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("--- Plotting Entropy vs. N ---\n")

# Create a sequence of N values (number of outcomes)
N_values <- seq(2, 20, by = 1)

# Calculate the entropy for each N
entropy_data <- data.frame(
  N = N_values,
  entropy = log2(N_values)
)

# Create the plot showing the relationship between N and Entropy
entropy_plot <- ggplot(entropy_data, aes(x = N, y = entropy)) +
  geom_line(color = "#3B82F6", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "#1D4ED8", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Entropy vs. Number of Outcomes (N)",
    subtitle = "Entropy increases logarithmically with the number of outcomes.",
    x = "Number of Outcomes (N)",
    y = expression(paste("Entropy ", H(Y), " (bits)"))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(entropy_plot)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 3: Visualization of PMF and Entropy
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n--- Plotting PMF for different N values ---\n")

# Create data for different N values
df_pmf <- data.frame(
  N = c(rep(4, 4), rep(6, 6), rep(10, 10)),
  outcome = c(1:4, 1:6, 1:10),
  probability = c(rep(1/4, 4), rep(1/6, 6), rep(1/10, 10))
)

# Calculate entropy for annotation
entropy_N4 <- round(log2(4), 2)
entropy_N6 <- round(log2(6), 2)
entropy_N10 <- round(log2(10), 2)

# Create the plot showing the PMF for different N values
pmf_plot <- ggplot(df_pmf, aes(x = as.factor(outcome), y = probability)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#3B82F6", color = "#1D4ED8", width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ N, scales = "free_x", labeller = as_labeller(function(N) paste0("N=", N))) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability Mass Function (PMF) and Entropy",
    subtitle = "As N increases, the PMF decreases, leading to higher entropy.",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Probability"
  ) +
  geom_text(data = data.frame(N = c(4, 6, 10),
                              label = c(paste("H(Y) = ", entropy_N4, "bits"), 
                                        paste("H(Y) = ", entropy_N6, "bits"), 
                                        paste("H(Y) = ", entropy_N10, "bits"))),
            aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = 1, vjust = 1.1, size = 4) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12))

print(pmf_plot)
```
